findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how _get_all_blocked_by preserves 'blocks'-edge targets that are NOT in the indexed node set (current code adds them unconditionally at _graph.py:151) so the reachability set is byte-identical after moving to adjacency-from-indexed-states.
evidence: _graph.py:151 `blocked.add(target)` runs for any 'blocks' target_id before any existence/filter check
load_indexed_states is defined as 'reduce_all + drop error/fsck + index by id' — dangling/dropped targets are absent from it
plan claims the refactor is 'behavior-identical (same nodes, same filtering)'
findings.finding: The plan's 'build adjacency once from indexed states, then bfs' for _get_all_blocked_by can change the result SET: the current implementation unconditionally does blocked.add(target) for every 'blocks' dep target (_graph.py:151) regardless of whether that target is an existing/reducible/non-error node, whereas load_indexed_states drops error/fsck (and possibly session-log) nodes, so a 'blocks' edge pointing at a dropped/nonexistent target would no longer be added to the blocked set.
scenarios: A ticket has a 'blocks' dep whose target_id is a deleted/nonexistent/error/session-log ticket; check_would_create_cycle relies on that target being present in _get_all_blocked_by's returned set
findings.suggested_fix: State that the adjacency for blocked-by must include 'blocks' edge targets even when the target has no indexed node (mirroring the current unconditional add), rather than intersecting edges with the indexed key set.
